result.summary: CreatorNudgeService (272 lines) has 22 distinct decision branches across getSuggestion / markDismissed / markActed, and currently has ZERO unit tests — the only test in service/creatorcopilot/ is CreatorMetaOAuthServiceTest.java. I read the service in full plus CreatorNudgeLog, CreatorNudgeLogRepository, TrendRepository, Trend, CreatorProfile, CreatorCopilotProperties, ThemeMatchService, CreatorSuggestionAiClient, CreatorCopilotDtos, CreatorCopilotController and V20260721140000__creator_nudge_log.sql. I propose 34 test methods in a new CreatorNudgeServiceTest.java following CreatorMetaOAuthServiceTest's exact conventions (@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class), package-private class, @Mock fields, @DisplayName + snake-ish method names, eq()/isNull() arg-by-arg verifies). THE HEADLINE FINDING IS NOT A MISSING TEST: the catch (DataIntegrityViolationException) at L160-170 is dead code. CreatorNudgeLog's @Id is caller-assigned (Ulids.newUlid(), L149), the entity has no @Version and does not implement Persistable, so Spring Data's isNew() is false and SimpleJpaRepository.save() calls em.merge() — which schedules the INSERT and returns without flushing. The uq_creator_nudge_day violation therefore fires at commit, inside the @Transactional proxy AFTER the try block has exited, so the catch can never run in production; a real concurrent first-of-day race produces a 500 today, exactly the outcome the comment at L163-165 claims to prevent. Worse, even if it did fire there, the persistence context would already be rollback-only and the recovery query at L166-167 would itself throw. Two tests are still proposed for that branch, but explicitly labelled path-only — they prove the mapping wiring, not the race, and must never be cited as evidence the cap-race is handled. Second finding: props.isEnabled() is never consulted in this service, so CREATOR_COPILOT_ENABLED=false (the prod default in both composes) gates only the jobs — the endpoint still serves, and with no tagging job it returns pending_tagging forever. Third: because nothing in Java writes to the trends table, the activeTrends.isEmpty() path is currently the ONLY reachable path in the deployed system. Mockito hazards that would make these tests lie are enumerated in risks — chiefly that every never()-verify against the AI client must use verifyNoInteractions or any(), never anyString(), because trendText comes from a mocked Trend and can legitimately be null.

risks: MOCKITO NULL-MATCHER TRAP (the F-0775 hazard, live in this file): every never()-verify against aiClient MUST be verifyNoInteractions(aiClient) or verify(aiClient, never()).requestSuggestion(any(), any(), any()). The verify would pass against code that really did call the AI client. Same rule for verify(creatorNudgeLogRepository, never()).save(any()): use any(), not a typed/isA matcher.

THE DataIntegrityViolationException CATCH AT L160-170 IS DEAD CODE. Caller-assigned @Id (L149) + no @Version + no Persistable => Spring Data isNew()==false => em.merge(), which schedules the INSERT without flushing; the uq_creator_nudge_day violation fires at commit, outside the try. The two proposed tests for that branch prove mapping wiring ONLY and must carry a javadoc saying so. As shipped, a genuine concurrent first-of-day request produces a 500 — precisely what the comment at L163-165 claims to prevent. And even if the exception did arrive in the catch, the recovery read at L166-167 would run on a rollback-only, poisoned persistence context and throw.

MockitoExtension default strictness is STRICT_STUBS. Do NOT stub in @BeforeEach the way CreatorMetaOAuthServiceTest does — the guard tests (profile-not-found, pending_tagging, no-active-trends) never touch most collaborators and would fail with UnnecessaryStubbingException. Stub per test.

result.summary: The n8n workflow (trendspark/n8n/trend-pull-workflow.json, 451 lines) is a 4-source fan-out (TMDb upcoming IN, NewsAPI top-headlines IN/entertainment, YouTube videos.list mostPopular IN, and a Google-Trends node that is a deliberate STUB returning []), an append-merge, a normalizer that shapes each payload into {text, source, category}, an inline "Theme Tagger + row builder" Code node, a MySQL INSERT of exactly 12 columns into `trends`, and a SEPARATE 06:30 IST trigger running `DELETE FROM trends WHERE expires_at < UTC_TIMESTAMP(6)`. Critically, the Java side ALREADY owns half the tagger: ThemeMatchService (influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/trendspark/ThemeMatchService.java) loads trendspark/theme-taxonomy.json at @PostConstruct and its themesForText(String) is byte-for-byte the JS KEYWORD_TO_THEMES containment match plus the closed-vocab filter — I verified the two vocabularies are identical (40 themes, 57 keyword mappings, no diff) by running `node trendspark/n8n/tagger-sync.check.js` (ALL PASS, 11 checks) and diffing the module against the JSON in node. So the keyword tagger must NOT be re-ported; it must be called. What is NOT in Java is deriveCampaignType — nothing loads influora-api/src/main/resources/trendspark/campaign-rulebook.json, which is on the classpath but has zero Java readers. Outbound HTTP: this repo has two established idioms and both are needed — Spring `RestClient`, lazily built inside a synchronized block, absolute URI hand-built (MetaGraphApiClient.java L48-77 and buildUri at L154-200, whose javadoc documents why UriBuilder.path() must not be used) for third-party GETs, and plain `java.net.http.HttpClient` pinned to HTTP/1.1, never-throws, returns null on any failure (TrendSparkAiClient.java) for the internal influora-ai leg. Job conventions from CreatorThemeTaggingJob/CreatorCaptionSyncJob: @Scheduled(cron = "${...}", zone = "UTC") + @SchedulerLock, flag check as the literal first statement with an info log and a bare return, per-item try/catch, and one summary log line of counters at the end. THE BLOCKER: the expiry DELETE cannot be ported as written. V20260721140000__creator_nudge_log.sql:33 adds `CONSTRAINT fk_creator_nudge_log_trend FOREIGN KEY (trend_id) REFERENCES trends (id)` with no ON DELETE clause, so InnoDB defaults to RESTRICT; that migration postdates the workflow. The moment the Co-pilot logs one suggestion, the single bulk DELETE fails with MySQL 1451 and rolls back entirely, so nothing ever expires. ON DELETE CASCADE is not the fix — creator_nudge_log's generated-column unique key is the per-creator/day cap backstop, and cascading would let a creator be re-nudged. Recommendation is soft expiry (TrendRepository.findActive already filters expiresAt > :now and both readers go through it).

Body, in order: (1) for each of the three TrendSourceClients, skip if !isConfigured() (count skipped), else fetch() and count ok/failed — a client never throws so one dead source cannot sink the run; (2) if every configured source returned empty, log WARN and return WITHOUT writing; (3) tag each RawTrend via TrendThemeTagger; (4) for rows whose themes are empty, call TrendTagRecoveryClient at most props.getMaxRecoveryPerRun() (40) times per run, stamping theme_source=AI_RECOVERED on success and DROPPING the row on null; (5) within-run dedup on the key `region + "|" + detectedDate + "|" + trendText.trim().toLowerCase()` in a HashSet, exactly the JS key; (6) cap to props.getMaxRowsPerRun() (100) AFTER dedup, first-N in input order — the JS comment is explicit that this is NOT a priority sort because no row has a priority field — logging the dropped count at WARN; (7) hand the list to TrendIngestWriter. Final log.info with sourcesOk/sourcesSkipped/sourcesFailed/fetched/tagged/recovered/droppedNoThemes/deduped/capped/written. All three HTTP fetches and all recovery calls happen with NO transaction open.

result.summary: Adversarial review of (a) adding NEWSAPI_KEY / TMDB_API_KEY / YOUTUBE_API_KEY to the influora-api config chain and (b) a Java @Scheduled outbound pull that writes into `trends`. The design is not fundamentally unsafe, but four things in the current tree make it worse than it looks. (1) Secret handling: `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists `env.example` BY PATH, so a real key committed there is invisible — I proved this empirically (three real-shaped keys in `influora-api/env.example` → 0 findings; the same three in `application.yml` → 3 findings), and the two tracked example files already carry what look like live Anthropic, Sarvam and R2 credentials that the scanner has never reported. On top of that the repo's own gate `.proof-os/gates/F-0206-gitleaks-baseline.sh` already exits 1 today (7 findings), so a new leak would not change the verdict — the gate is vacuous for this change. (2) Two of the three keys ride in the QUERY STRING (TMDb `api_key`, YouTube `key`), and `logback-spring.xml` is a single CONSOLE appender at root INFO whose pattern ends in `%wEx` — full stack traces to stdout, into docker json-file logs on a box shared with a neighbouring project. Any log line or exception carrying the request URI leaks the key. (3) The outbound calls: there is NO Java SSRF/response-size helper to reuse (the only `ssrf_guard.py` is in influora-ai), every existing Java client uses unbounded `HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString()`, and the shared-box JVM is capped at `-Xmx900m` — a large or hostile upstream response is an OOM, and any redirect the client follows carries the query-string key to the redirect target. (4) The strongest finding is a trust-boundary one that survives the n8n-vs-Java decision: `trends` has no unique key and no writer-side validation, `ThemeMatchService.score` is a plain overlap count, and `CreatorNudgeService.templatedFallback` interpolates `trend.getTrendText()` VERBATIM into creator-facing copy with NO LLM and NO validator in the path. So one row whose `themes` lists the whole 40-term vocab, with a future `detected_date` (wins ties in the `score > bestScore` loop) and a distant `expires_at`, is a broadcast primitive: attacker-chosen text delivered to every creator who clears the threshold. The prompt-injection defences (`wrap_untrusted`, closed-vocab theme, output validators) are genuinely good, but they only guard the AI branch — the fallback branch bypasses all of them, and `parse_and_validate` has no URL/handle check even on the AI branch. On the neighbour's n8n: in the committed config it CANNOT write to our `trends` — neither utho compose publishes 3306, n8n is not a service in any prod compose, and README §7 says 3306 stays closed. What IS internet-reachable is `/internal/trendspark/tag`: the Caddyfile `{$AI_DOMAIN}` block proxies the whole host and `nginx-ai-influora.conf` has a bare `location /`, so that endpoint is exposed at https://ai.influora.in behind a single static shared secret, and the utho composes never set `WORKSPACE_DAILY_HARD_CAP_USD` — so the only real ceiling is the global `AI_DAILY_SPEND_CEILING_USD=15.0` shared with Meera chat.
